items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: Errol Garner was another one. But when I heard the guitar players, especially Wes, then I started hearing Jimmy Smith

ctx.x: Or you figure out who you don’t want to steal from along the way too.

That’s basically I think probably what happens really. That doesn’t interest me, I won’t steal from him. Now this over here, yes, let me grab some of that. Well you know I grew up listening to, when I really became interested in music, you know I was telling you about being from the family of pianists, I think that really actually turned me off in the beginning because I hated piano lessons. You know because everybody did that. But they were smart, after about a year they said listen, if you don’t like that you…

of course all of the bands of that time, and the guitar player with James Brown and the whole smear of kind of those two kinds of music, I even had a little period of time where I listened to a lot of country music. And basically because I loved the guitar playing, I loved their sound, I loved their percussive attack and the edge they played with, and I got into a little country thing for a while. But then I kind of gravitated back to the jazz world and I was hearing Wes Montgomery. That’s one of the first, I…
